title: Security onboarding verification checklist and scope decisions for Private Deploy KMS/HSM + SSO/RBAC
creator: Lena Morris
description:
Purpose: produce a concise, actionable verification worksheet that teams (Solutions, Ops, Eng, and Customer Success) can follow to validate customer private deployments for KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML federation, RBAC, and audit logging before handoff.

Scope: Private/VPC and on-prem deployments only. This ticket covers: requirements clarification, scope decisions for minimal acceptance, the evidence checklist for sign-off, and a small set of remediation playbooks if an item fails validation. Out of scope: Hosted API onboarding, runtime kernel-level audit logs, and entitlement billing flows.

Context & Motivation: Customers onboarding Private deployments require auditable verification of crypto custody (KMS/HSM), identity federation (SAML/OIDC), role and admin boundaries (RBAC), and read/writeable, tamper-evident audit logs. Historically sign-off has been ad-hoc; this ticket aims to standardize acceptance criteria, reduce back-and-forth, and shorten time-to-production.

How this doc will be used: Solutions engineers will run the checklist during onboarding, Eng will validate acceptance artifacts and mark items Done, Security and Compliance will sign off where indicated. The artifact must be machine-readable (spreadsheet template + human-friendly worksheet) and include links to automated verification scripts where available.
acceptance_criteria:
1) All mandatory checklist rows marked PASS with attached evidence links (screenshots, logs, PRs).
2) KMS/HSM: Customer key policies verified, HSM attestation or KMS IAM policy exported, and monthly rotation policy confirmed.
3) SSO/SAML: SAML metadata validated, assertion signature verification, user provisioning or SCIM (if required) tested in staging.
4) RBAC: Role definitions present, at least two non-owner admin roles tested, separation of duties documented.
5) Audit Logs: Admin and data-plane events are being emitted, retention policy meets customer's contractual requirement, tamper-evidence (checksum/immutable store) validated.
6) Remediation plan exists for any FAIL items and is scheduled as dependency.
7) Security review checklist ticked and sign-off recorded from Security and Solutions.
8) Ticket closed with links to artifacts: PRD, design diagram, GitHub PRs, onboarding spreadsheet, and the deployment runbook.
signoff_checklist: KMS/HSM key lifecycle documentation attached (policies + rotation schedule)
HSM attestation or KMS audit trail exported and validated
Customer key import or generate flow tested in staging
SAML metadata and certificates uploaded; assertion verification test passed
SSO provisioning or SCIM flows demonstrated (if included in scope)
Admin and operator RBAC roles created and tested (no owner-privilege abuse)
Least-privilege access documented for support and ops teams
Audit logs: admin-auth, config-changes, model-serving access, and key usage are present
Audit retention and export policy matches contract (date-stamped evidence)
Immutable storage or checksum mechanism for logs verified
Security review completed and signed by Security team (name + date)
Solutions engineer acceptance noted and customer confirmation attached
Backout and incident runbook exists for crypto/identity failures
Open dependencies listed and assigned with ETA
decisions: Decision 1: For initial adoption we will require either HSM attestation OR customer-managed cloud KMS with customer-managed CMEK; hybrid option accepted with explicit evidence. Trade-off: reduces friction vs. strict HSM-only requirement.
Decision 2: SCIM provisioning is optional unless the customer requests automated provisioning; manual provisioning with audit trail is acceptable as a temporary measure.
Decision 3: Retention default set to 90 days for non-PHI customers; customers with regulatory needs will specify contractual retention and will trigger extended retention architecture work.
Decision 4: RBAC baseline must include at minimum: Owner, Admin, Operator, Support (read-only), Auditor. Fine-grained perms can be iterated post-onboarding.

Decision 5: Evidence types accepted: signed screenshots with timestamp + exported logs + GitHub PR referencing the onboarding ticket. Live Console view links must include a timestamped audit event where possible.
open_questions: Q1: For air-gapped on-prem customers, do we require HSM hardware attestation on day-0 or can it be deferred to the first quarterly audit?
Q2: Should we require automated log export to the customer's SIEM for all enterprise customers by default? (cost/complexity trade-off)
Q3: Are there legal constraints on storing HSM attestation artifacts in our control plane for EU customers?
Q4: Which exact set of model-serving events must be included in the 'data-plane' audit log for regulatory customers? Need mapping from Legal/Compliance.
